## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
An open license (e.g. MIT, BSD, Apache 2.0, CC BY, CC0) allowing reuse, modification and redistribution is stated for all components the authors created (code and data alike), in the README, a LICENSE file, or the repository metadata. For third-party data the authors cannot relicense, the original terms of use are stated.

[Supported by: Permissive/open license: [#3](../../sources.qmd#p3 "Reproducing statistical results") (attribution-only open licensing), [#20](../../sources.qmd#p20 "Successes and struggles with computational reproducibility: lessons from the fragile families challenge") MIT, [#99](../../sources.qmd#p99 "Introducing reproducible research standards at the world bank") MIT/BSD3, [#108](../../sources.qmd#p108 "Checklists for computational reproducibility in social sciences: insights from literature and survey evaluation") MIT/Apache/CC BY, [#54](../../sources.qmd#p54 "WORCS: a workflow for open reproducible code in science") CC BY default, [#77](../../sources.qmd#p77 "Report of the AEA data editor") CC BY default, [#83](../../sources.qmd#p83 "Reproducibility and transparency versus privacy and confidentiality: Reflections from a data editor") open license required by AEA, [#120](../../sources.qmd#p120 "Reproducibility spectrum for applied social sciences: conceptual taxonomy and recommended tools") CC BY/CC0. Separate code + data licenses: [#45](../../sources.qmd#p45 "Toward reusable science with readable code and reproducibility"). All elements: [#35](../../sources.qmd#p35 "Trust, but verify: an investigation of methods of verification and dissemination of computational research artifacts for transparency and reproducibility"). Presence check: [#93](../../sources.qmd#p93 "Unintended code errors and computational reproducibility"), [#66](../../sources.qmd#p66 "Reproducible research publication workflow: a canonical workflow framework and FAIR digital object approach to quality research output"), [#19](../../sources.qmd#p19 "The ReproRubric: evaluation criteria for the reproducibility of computational analyses").]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
A license is stated, but it is not open (it restricts reuse, modification or redistribution of material the authors created), or a license is stated for only some components of the package (e.g. for the code but not the data).

[Supported by: [#45](../../sources.qmd#p45 "Toward reusable science with readable code and reproducibility") one license missing (code or data) creates legal uncertainty. [#34](../../sources.qmd#p34 "Reproducibility and replicability in economics") data license prevents redistribution.]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
No license is stated in the package.

[Supported by: [#45](../../sources.qmd#p45 "Toward reusable science with readable code and reproducibility") 'no license ... means that all copyright laws apply', [#48](../../sources.qmd#p48 "Challenges of curating for reproducible and FAIR research output") unclear usage license as a barrier.]{.source-note}
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never.
:::

## Text evidence (30 quotes)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal" title="Show quotes"}
**[#3](../../sources.qmd#p3)** Reproducing statistical results · *injunctive*

> "Terms of use and licensing. Ideally code and data default to open; that is, they are published under a permissive reuse license" (p. 11); and "I suggest that scholarly objects be made openly available using the Reproducible Research Standard... which recommends attribution-only open licensing for code, data, and the research article" (p. 13)

---

**[#14](../../sources.qmd#p14)** An empirical analysis of journal policy effectiveness for computational reproducibility · *injunctive*

> "Any restrictions on the availability of data, codes, or materials, including fees and original data obtained from other sources... must be disclosed to the editors upon submission" (p.2584)

---

**[#19](../../sources.qmd#p19)** The ReproRubric: evaluation criteria for the reproducibility of computational analyses · *injunctive*

> Materials and/or code is licensed using an approved license

---

**[#20](../../sources.qmd#p20)** Successes and struggles with computational reproducibility: lessons from the fragile families challenge · *injunctive*

> "The code should be released under the MIT license, but we will consider other permissive licenses in special situations" (footnote 12, p.6)

---

**[#32](../../sources.qmd#p32)** Beyond open data: a model for linking digital artifacts to enable reproducibility of scientific claims · *injunctive*

> "The preceding discussion is predicated on the author having the ability and legal rights to share data and code associated with claims" (p. 11)

---

**[#34](../../sources.qmd#p34)** Reproducibility and replicability in economics · *injunctive*

> "Some widely used data sets are accessible by any researcher, but the license they are subject to prevents their redistribution and thus their inclusion as part of data deposits." (p. 15)

---

**[#35](../../sources.qmd#p35)** Trust, but verify: an investigation of methods of verification and dissemination of computational research artifacts for transparency and reproducibility · *injunctive*

> "License and copyright information should be provided for all elements of the package. Although not strictly required for reproducibility assessment, license and copyright are important for future reusability" (p.170)

---

**[#38](../../sources.qmd#p38)** Ten simple rules for writing dockerfiles for reproducible data science · *injunctive*

> "Regarding licensing information, this should include the license of your own code and could point to a LICENSE file within the image" (p. 11-12)

---

**[#39](../../sources.qmd#p39)** How to make a pie: reproducible research for empirical economics and econometrics · *injunctive*

> "the choice of the versioning tool should satisfy the data terms of use" (p. 1147)

---

**[#45](../../sources.qmd#p45)** Toward reusable science with readable code and reproducibility · *injunctive*

> "Our form features both data and code license fields as different types of licenses apply to these resources. The absence of one of the two licenses in a replication package with data and code may create legal uncertainty. Though the licenses should be open to allow reuse, no license within the published material means that all copyright laws apply and that the author retains all rights to data or code. To create a platform that facilitates reusable research, licenses for both types of resources needed to be incorporated." (p. 4)

*Note:* only check presence of the license file, not the content

---

**[#48](../../sources.qmd#p48)** Challenges of curating for reproducible and FAIR research output · *injunctive*

> "Inability to access data when conditions of use are unclear" (p.20) and "Unclear usage license" (p.21)

---

**[#51](../../sources.qmd#p51)** A reproducible data analysis workflow with R Markdown, Git, Make, and Docker · *injunctive*

---
